Engine shops at Hartsfield and the airlifter plant in Marietta: SNT-TC-1A and NAS 410 for Atlanta NDT careers

Atlanta's aerospace NDT jobs come from two very different kinds of employer. Airline technical operations and component shops around Hartsfield-Jackson overhaul engines and parts for the fleet, and Lockheed Martin's plant in Marietta builds the C-130J. Around both sit suppliers, power plants and fabricators with their own rules. Which personnel standard your certification follows depends on which of these you join. The full side-by-side is in NAS 410 vs SNT-TC-1A.

The airline engine and component shops

Delta TechOps holds FAA repair station certificate DALR026A and an EASA Part-145 approval. Under Part 145 the FAA approves the station, not the technician, and its Advisory Circular 65-31B accepts NAS 410, ATA Specification 105, SNT-TC-1A and several other standards. What matters for a candidate is the personnel standard written into the station's manual, which its NDT Level 3 can name. Stations that hold an EASA approval alongside the FAA certificate also work with EASA guidance, which points to EN 4179, the European twin of NAS 410. Smaller repair stations near the airport make the same choice in their own manuals, so do not assume two shops use one document.

The C-130J line in Marietta and the shops that supply it

Lockheed Martin's inspectors in Marietta certify under the company's own written practice; ask its Level 3 which standard and revision it names. The suppliers that machine, form, finish and test parts for military airframe programs are where the answer is most predictable. NAS 410 replaced MIL-STD-410 on defense contracts in 1998, and primes routinely write it into supplier quality clauses, so a Georgia machine shop or special process house on that work should expect NAS 410 and, if accredited, Nadcap AC7114 audits of its personnel files.

Power plants, fabricators and the code side

Plant Vogtle's units, the coal stations Georgia Power keeps running, and the metro's pressure vessel and structural fabricators work to ASME and AWS requirements. Those codes call for personnel certified to SNT-TC-1A or, on some contracts, CP-189. Nuclear owners add their own quality-assurance requirements on top. A technician can spend years on this side and then cross to an engine shop, but the certification is reissued by the new employer.

Where ASNT's central certificates fit

Atlanta candidates can sit ASNT's central examinations without leaving the metro. Those certificates are third-party credentials, useful as evidence, but neither employer-based scheme is replaced by them. An ASNT NDT Level III certificate has long been credited toward the NAS 410 Level 3 general examination; it does not make the holder a NAS 410 Level 3, and the employer's specific and practical examinations still apply. Our ASNT Level III training page explains that route.

An Atlanta candidate's short list

  1. Ask which document and revision the written practice follows, and who the Responsible Level 3 (RL3) is, or which Level III approves the written practice.
  2. Bring course outlines with recorded hours, a signed experience log split by method, examination results and a current vision record. Those are what get credited.
  3. If the program is written to NAS 410, expect to add formal penetrant and magnetic particle training, because NAS 410 asks for more documented training in the surface methods than SNT-TC-1A recommends.
  4. For engine work, start logging eddy current and penetrant hours early; see eddy current testing in aviation.

For Atlanta suppliers and repair stations

Name the governing standard and revision on every certification. If you serve both aerospace and industrial customers, keep the programs plainly separate. Move any NAS 410 program to Revision 6, released in December 2025, on your customers' timetable, updating training material and examination banks with it. Auditors pick individual inspectors and trace each one to evidence. Atlantis prepares and reviews NAS 410 audit documentation that your RL3 then approves, and Atlanta firms can use our aerospace NDT consulting for written practices built on SNT-TC-1A, aligned to the customer's flow-down and Nadcap AC7114.

Atlantis for the Atlanta metro

Training follows ASNT SNT-TC-1A: theory online at your own pace with an ASNT NDT Level III answering questions, practice in the Practical NDT simulator, and the hands-on work and practical examination at your employer's facility under its written practice. There is no Atlantis classroom in Atlanta. Check your theory first with the free Level II practice tests. Georgia plants and fabricators can bring in Atlantis for UT, MT, PT and VT inspection.

The boundary, for anyone in Georgia reading this: Atlantis does not provide NAS 410 training, certification, examinations or a Responsible Level 3. Whether SNT-TC-1A-based coursework counts toward a NAS 410 certification is your employer's RL3's decision; raise it before you enroll. More on how those programs work is in NAS 410 explained.
